found: sess425 (ccloop c7ee71c6), 2026-08-28: design-consult audit item (c) of the D-0341 ruling ('cancel/release during PENDING_DURABLE'), proven by usermode reproducer tests/tauth/concurrent_release_test scenario 5 on the 0.35.1 engine before the fix
summary: On the TCP transport with the durable authority ledger, a LOCAL requester on the master whose retry budget runs out while its grant is PENDING_DURABLE (decided, ledger commit in flight — e.g. carried by a slow release transition) leaves the master holding a durable grant nobody claims: the timeout path correctly refuses to free a non-WAITING entry (P4G-TIMEOUT-FREE-ALIAS state=5), the commit then lands, dlm_txn_finalize marks the entry GRANTED and signals a waiter that no longer exists — and ignores that nothing was signalled. The master node now 'holds' the resource (EX in the reproducer: platter ex=<master>) with no thread that will ever unlock it: every other node's request blocks until the master happens to request the same resource again (the already-granted shortcut adopts the orphan) or unmounts. The remote analogue (an unsolicited GRANT at a node with no waiter) already answers LOCK_RELEASE; the local one had no driver. Same invariant class as D-0341: every durable authority must have exactly one live master-owned driver.
mechanism: dlm/dlm.c dlm_txn_finalize deliver loop: `if (it->signal_local) pending_signal_resource(ctx, res, mode, 0, 0);` — the bool return (false = no pending waiter for the resource) was discarded. dlm_lock_impl's timeout unlink (P4G guard) frees only WAITING/BLOCKED entries with the matching pend_waiter; promote_waiters cleared pend_waiter at decision time, so a PENDING_DURABLE entry survives the requester's departure by design (the committing thread delivers). Reproduced: B (remote) holds EX; M (master, local) queues EX with a 1-attempt budget (1000 ms); B's release — whose transition carries M's grant — is delayed 1600 ms (ledger commit_delay_once_ms): M times out (-110), the commit lands, platter ex=1000 (M), B's next EX never granted (lock_wait 2000 ms, done=0).
